title: Cap. X Arg. VIII: Augustine stops Pelagians/Semipelagians with elect/reprobate infants; De praed. sanct. 12 and De bono pers. 11 — God helps those little ones he chose before the world
pass_a_gloss: By this argument drawn from the election of certain infants, the reprobation of certain, Augustine everywhere stops the mouths of the Pelagians and Semipelagians, who recalled this discrimination of elect and non-elect unto the foreseen acts of human wills, whether good or evil, just as the Arminians now also recall it. It would be endless to heap up all Augustine’s testimonies unto this sentence. See De Praed. Sanct. cap. 12, De bono persev. cap. 11. where he expressly asserts, God succours little ones, whom he wills, even when not willing nor running; whom namely he elected before the foundation of the world; but those whom he wills not, he does not succour, concerning whom in his predestination he judged otherwise, secretly indeed, but justly.
pass_b_english: From this argument—election of some infants, reprobation of others—Augustine everywhere stops the mouths of Pelagians and Semipelagians, who traced the divide of elect and non-elect to foreseen acts of human wills, good or evil, as the Arminians now do. It would be endless to pile up all his witnesses on this point. See De praedestinatione sanctorum 12 and De bono perseverantiae 11, where he expressly asserts: God helps the little ones he wills, even when they are not willing or running—those he chose before the foundation of the world; those he does not will, he does not help, of whom in his predestination he judged otherwise, secretly but justly.
source_text: Hoc argumento ab infantium quorundam electione, quorundam reprobatione, petito Augustinus passim obstruit ora Pelagianorum et Semipelagianorum, qui hoc discrimen electorum et non-electorum ad praevisos actus humanarum voluntatum sive bonos sive malos revocarunt, sicuti et Arminiani jam revocant. Infinitum esset omnia Augustini testimonia in hanc sententiam accumulare. Videte De Praed. Sanct. cap. 12, De bono persev. cap. 11. ubi diserte asserit, Deus parvulis, quibus vult, etiam non volentibus neque currentibus subvenire; quos scilicet ante constitutionem mundi elegit; quibus vero non vult non subvenire, de quibus in sua praedestinatione occulte quidem, sed juste aliud judicavit.
notes: Densify De praedestinatione Cap. X Arg. VII cont. section 744. Pass A!=B. Packet praedestinatione_cap10_arg7_densify.
